title: Corrections
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units

outcomes: Understand how the corrections subsystem fits into the whole system of criminal justice.
Identify the primary differences between jails, prisons, juvenile halls, and probation camps.
Have a clear understanding of the juvenile justice system as it relates to delinquent, dependent, and status offenders.
Explain the juvenile court concept of least restrictive alternative.
Distinguish the basic difference between an interview with an interrogation.
Understand the purposes and goals of different correctional system programs offered to inmates such as educational programs, health programs, life skills, religious programs, and vocational programs.
Describe the three components of the criminal justice system: Explain the relationship
between the police, courts and corrections.
Understand the problems of parolees, and describe how they differ from those of probationers. Describe the concept of prisonization.
Explain the problem involved in confining elderly criminals, female prisoners, and the mentally ill prisoners.
Compare and contrast the difference between how adults, juveniles, gays, homosexuals, lesbians, and cross-gender persons are handled by the criminal justice system: Explain why this is important.
Understand the basic rights each inmate is entitled to under the 1st, 4th, 8th, and 14th Amendments.
Understand the conflicting roles of being a cop and social worker as a Probation Officer and Parole agent.

notes: Catalog codes with leading zeros (ADM JUS 008, 039, 075; CORR 002) were matched to closed-list codes ADM JUS 8, 39, 75 and CORR 2.

Outcome 8 is split across a page break: '8. Describe the three components of the criminal justice system: Explain the relationship' continues as '9. between the police, courts and corrections.' The catalog numbers the continuation as item 9; recorded as two entries as printed. A reviewer may consider these one outcome.

The description mentions entry-level employment in any juvenile or adult correctional facility and supervision by a Corrections Officer; only 'Corrections field' was recorded as a career named for the program.
